title: 7 Dating Rules I Learned the Hard Way After Divorce

items.headline: Being wanted is flattering. Being needed is a job.
items.body: Ask her to be exclusive on date four and she doesn't hear "I like you." She hears "please don't send me back to that empty apartment."

items.headline: You're running dial-up in a broadband world.
items.body: Ten years of marriage taught you one move: lock it in. The game changed while you were inside. Update the software before you play.

items.headline: Attention is not commitment.
items.body: Chemistry is not character. Access is not reciprocity. She let you into the building. She never gave you a key.

items.headline: Stop asking if she likes you. Ask if you like her.
items.body: Am I attracted to her, or to being wanted? Do I like her, or do I like not being alone on a Thursday? Ask it on every drive home.

items.headline: Slow the exclusivity clock all the way down.
items.body: At four dates you know her presentation, not her. Watch her handle something going wrong first. If she's worth locking in now, she still will be in a month.

items.headline: Don't cancel your life for a maybe.
items.body: Keep the training session, the poker night, dinner with your kid. A man who clears his calendar for a third date just told her how much life he has.

items.headline: You can't fake having options.
items.body: A performance of abundance is just neediness in a costume. Build a life you'd genuinely pick over her approval. That's the only version that works.

cta.headline: Be a man with options.
body: A life full of them. Not a phone.
